A.P. Moller - Maersk reported a group ROIC of 12.3% for 2024, which was above its yearly target of above 7.5% under normalised conditions. Profitability lagged in the first half of 2024, but the strong second-half result brought ROIC above target. The measure is defined as profit/loss before financial items for the year (EBIT) less tax on EBIT, divided by the average invested capital over the last twelve months.

ArcelorMittal reported a group-wide LTIFR of 0.70 for 2024 (Sustainable development, Performance in 2024). LTIFR is defined as Lost Time Injuries per 1,000,000 worked hours, covering both own personnel and contractors (Glossary). A lost time injury (LTI) is an incident causing an injury that prevents the person from returning to his/her next scheduled shift or work period (Glossary).
Roughly 11% — Maersk had more than 12,000 seafarers out of 108,160 employees at year-end 2024.

Catch volume fell from 75 893 tonnes in 2023 to 64 991 tonnes in 2024 (a decrease of 10 902 tonnes), reflecting quota cuts of 34% for cod, 43% for haddock and 6% for saithe in the northern zone [1][2]. The Board says earnings in the WildCatch segment have been significantly affected by the low quota basis and will remain so for some time, expecting 2025 and probably also 2026 to be challenging for the segment [3]. The quota reduction is to some extent offset by higher prices, though these challenge the land-based industry, which made a larger loss in 2024 than 2023 [2].
